transcript.text: Is it normal for my dishwasher to leave everything wet? Plastic tubs are soaking every time and there's drips on the glasses. It's a Bosch Serie 4.

Partly, yes. Plastic tubs coming out wet is very common and largely normal. Plastic holds very little heat, so water doesn't evaporate off it the way it does from hot china. Bosch machines like the Serie 4 dry by condensation rather than blowing hot air, so plastics always come off worst. Drips on glasses are a bit different, though. That usually points to rinse aid being low or the dose set too low. Rinse aid is what makes water sheet off instead of sitting in droplets. Most likely causes, in order:
1. Rinse aid empty or set too low (the biggest single factor for drying).
2. Programme and door habits. Eco and quick programmes dry very little, and condensation drying needs time.
3. Loading. Upturned tubs and cups with hollow bases collect water and tip it onto the glasses when you unload. A genuine fault (the machine not heating) is much less likely. It would show as dishes coming out cold, not just wet. Things to check:
1. Look at the rinse-aid cap or indicator next to the detergent flap and top it up if it's low. If it's full, raise the dosage setting a notch or two (it's in the machine's settings; your manual shows how). If the drips on the glasses clear up, that was it.
2. Note which programme you use. If it's Eco or quick, try Auto or Normal for a load or two. If drying improves noticeably, it's the programme, not a fault.
3. At the end, leave it 20–30 minutes before unloading, or crack the door open a little to let the steam out. Unload the bottom basket first so water from upturned tubs on top doesn't drip down onto the dry items.
4. Load plastics tilted, on the top basket, rather than flat or nested. The key thing that separates normal drying from a fault is this: when the cycle finishes, are the dishes hot and steamy, or cold? Hot but wet is a drying issue that the steps above should sort. Cold dishes and poorer washing would point to a heating problem instead. And is there rinse aid in it at the moment?

The dishes are hot and steamy at the end, so it's heating fine. The rinse aid is empty, the symbol is lit, but I use all-in-one tablets. I always use Eco 50 and open the door straight away when it finishes.

Hot and steamy at the end means it's heating properly, so this isn't a fault. All-in-one tablets do contain some rinse aid, but it's only a small amount and it's released with the rest of the tablet early in the wash. Very little of it is left for the final hot rinse, which is where it does its job. Lots of people find drying improves a lot once they fill the rinse-aid compartment anyway, even with all-in-ones, and Bosch machines rely on it heavily because they dry by condensation. The lit symbol is just the machine telling you it's empty. On top of that, Eco 50 is the weakest programme for drying. It runs cooler, so there's less heat in the load to drive the water off. 1. Fill the rinse-aid compartment with ordinary dishwasher rinse aid. Wipe up any spill, as it foams. If the glasses come out without drips after a couple of loads, that was the main cause. If you still see drips, raise the rinse-aid dose a notch in the settings.
2. Keep Eco 50 if you like the savings, but see whether your machine has an Extra Dry or similar drying option (not every Serie 4 does; check the buttons or the manual). Alternatively, run Auto or a 65° programme once to compare. Much drier results would confirm the programme is a big part of it.
3. Opening the door at the end is fine and helps steam escape. Just open it a few centimetres and leave it 20–30 minutes before unloading, rather than unloading straight away. That gives the residual heat time to evaporate the water. Even with all that, expect plastic tubs to come out a bit damp. That's normal for any condensation-drying machine. It would only be worth looking further if the glasses and china were still soaking with full rinse aid on a hotter programme, or if the dishes ever came out cold.

candidates: Low or empty rinse aid (or dose set too low) (high)
Normal condensation drying: plastics hold little heat, worse on Eco/quick programmes or if the door stays shut (high)
Loading: cups/tubs pooling water and dripping onto items below (medium)
Genuine heating fault (only if the wash is cold) (low)
